item.description: A metal (from Ancient Greek μέταλλον (métallon) 'mine, quarry, metal') is a material that, when polished or fractured, shows a lustrous appearance, and conducts electricity and heat relatively well. item.title: Metal | Definition, Characteristics, Types, & Facts | Britannica
item.description: Metal, any of a class of substances characterized by high electrical and thermal conductivity as well as by malleability, ductility, and high reflectivity of light. Approximately three-quarters of all known chemical elements are metals. Learn more about metals in this article.

item.title: METAL Definition & Meaning - Merriam-Webster
item.description: The meaning of METAL is any of various opaque, fusible, ductile, and typically lustrous substances that are good conductors of electricity and heat, form cations by loss of electrons, and yield basic oxides and hydroxides; especially : one that is a chemical element as distinguished from an alloy.

item.title: Types of Metals: Classifications, Properties, and Uses
item.description: The main types of metal used in manufacturing fall into four groups: ferrous metals such as steel and cast iron, non-ferrous metals such as aluminium, copper, and titanium, metal alloys such as brass and bronze, and precious metals such as gold, silver, and platinum.
